vulnerability.name: CVE-2019-1010022
vulnerability.description: glibc nptl: the stack guard can be bypassed by an attacker who already controls a stack buffer overflow

statements.impact_statement: glibc upstream treats it as a non-security bug and no real threat (sourceware bug 22850) and Debian records it as unimportant and permanently unfixed, so no libc6 update can ever clear this finding.
statements.status_notes: The product purl deliberately carries no version: Trivy reads that as any version of the package. The matching DEBIAN-CVE-2019-1010022 statement repeats this assessment for DevGuard, which keys its findings on the Debian OSV identifier rather than the CVE id.

statements.impact_statement: Same assessment as CVE-2019-1010022 above, under the identifier DevGuard reports the finding as.
statements.status_notes: DevGuard matches a version-less product purl against nothing, so the version is expressed as the constraint >=0.0.0-0, which its purl matcher reads as any version including Debian's revision suffixes.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-5450
vulnerability.description: glibc: scanf family with %mc and an explicit field width above 1024 overflows the heap buffer by one byte (GLIBC-SA-2026-0009)

statements.impact_statement: The image runs a single Java application on the JVM; neither it nor anything else shipped in the slim image calls the scanf family with the %mc conversion, which is the only way to reach the overflow.
statements.status_notes: See the DEBIAN-CVE-2026-5450 statement below for the same assessment under the identifier DevGuard uses.

statements.impact_statement: Same assessment as CVE-2026-5450 above, under the identifier DevGuard reports the finding as.
statements.status_notes: The version is expressed as the constraint >=0.0.0-0 so the statement keeps matching across libc6 updates; DevGuard does not match version-less product purls.
